subject.title: [Feature Request]: one-line local bootstrap for daemon + dashboard auth + Telegram owner setup

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class one-line local bootstrap surface for daemon, dashboard auth, and Telegram owner setup, and should that surface require numeric owner allowlists or allow resolved usernames/preapproval while keeping pairing explicit?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but the permanent public setup API and Telegram owner trust model are product/security choices rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Add explicit allowlist bootstrap
options.body: Create additive onboard/bootstrap flags that configure the daemon, dashboard URL, Telegram token, numeric owner allowlist, and ownerAllowFrom while keeping pairing approval explicit for other users.

options.title: Split into narrower issues
options.body: Keep this as an umbrella and land separate decisions for Telegram owner defaults, dashboard auth discoverability, and daemon setup composition.

options.title: Document composition only
options.body: Keep core setup surfaces separate and point users to documented commands or external scripts/prompts for advanced local stacks.

recommendation.title: Add explicit allowlist bootstrap
recommendation.body: Create additive onboard/bootstrap flags that configure the daemon, dashboard URL, Telegram token, numeric owner allowlist, and ownerAllowFrom while keeping pairing approval explicit for other users.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans setup UX, dashboard auth, and Telegram security policy, and this owner has the strongest recent cross-surface history plus timeline mention signal.
